newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, exports pressure nearbys.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, exports pressure nearbys.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed on Friday with nearbys down on mediocre USDA export sales figures while forecasts for cold temperatures lifted new crop, pit sources said.
"We had a low export sales number but it had been expected," said Dale Durchholz, analyst with Agrivisor Services, a subsidiary of the Illinois Farm Bureau.

"Everybody is pretty dialed into the fact that exports are going to fall because the South Americans are shipping it out as fast as they can," he added. "That's going to siphon some business away from the U.S."
USDA said U.S. net export sales of soybeans during the week ended May 8 totaled 141,200 tonnes, within the range of expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
November gained on forecasts for cold weather in the U.S. Midwest with Friday's temperatures forecast to fall into the high 20s F in parts of South Dakota, Minnesota and Iowa.
Still, some traders said it was too early to fixate on weather problems and pointed out that plantings were ahead of average. They also noted outlooks for a warm weekend.
Soybeans ended seven cents per bushel lower to one cent higher with July down 6-1/4 at $8.57-3/4.

Unwinding of bull spreads was the featured play on the day, keying off of the bearish export data and bullish weather. The July/November spread closed at $1.52-1/4, premium July, down 7-1/4 from Wednesday's close.
ING spread one million bushels November/July at $1.55 to $1.56, premium July and Refco Inc spread 0.5 million November/July at $1.55 to $1.57-1/2.

On the day, funds were again strong sellers with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer a seller of three million bushels July, pit sources said. Refco Inc sold 2.5 million November and one million July and Smith Barney sold one million July.
Cargill Inc bought one million July.
In options trade, Louis Dreyfus sold 200 July $8.50 puts at 17 to 17-1/2 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 400 July $9.75 calls at 2-1/2 to three cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 58,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 69,147.
